parsed.explanation: The combined regime is severe for trans visitors. National visa/passport screening treats sex as a birth binary, eliminates X markers, and can make document discrepancies grounds for refusal, stranding, or permanent fraud findings; airport checks may out travelers. In the division, birth-sex facility bans cover schools, colleges, and government buildings; ID mismatch can trigger ejection, arrest, or men’s custody, and immigration/correctional custody reports abuse. Adult-alone exposure is high if discovered; families with minors face care denial, provider criminalization, and school investigations. No execution, and imprisonment is not automatic, so the score stays above lowest anchors but below exclusion-only anchors because border, facilities, custody, and care are hostile with weak remedies.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visa screening treats sex as a birth binary; X markers barred for new issues; discrepancies can cause refusal, secondary screening, stranding, or permanent fraud ineligibility; airport security may force outing.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; active litigation and court uncertainty may limit some effects.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry mismatch can escalate into interrogation, refusal, detention, investigation, or custody placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; correctional policies cut hair, remove hormones, and impose conversion therapy; facility arrest included 24-hour men’s-ward placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law and constitutional claims exist; some orders are enjoined, but no documented visitor protection in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility or document dispute can move into investigation, immigration detention, or criminal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National bars congruent single-sex government facilities; division bans birth-sex facilities in public schools, colleges and government buildings, with binary-sex spaces allowed; some jurisdictions criminalize refusing to leave.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Other state/provinces and local ordinances provide protections, but not statewide in the division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Government buildings, schools, transit, clinics, and lodging checks can expose ID mismatch or force exclusion.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is criminalized; providers face a 10-year felony in the division; national reimbursement threats and school investigations narrow care access; no visitor continuity-care guarantee.
care_services.protection: Emergency care protections are not documented; national employment or hate-crime law does not secure treatment continuity.
care_services.interaction: HRT continuity, illness, or a child’s care-seeking may cause denial, records exposure, provider liability, or guardian inquiries.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Officials frame trans rights as fraudulent gender ideology; police are directed to investigate schools and prosecute teachers; counterterrorism language links pro-transgender ideology to violent groups; no state gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute and courts can intervene; civil-liberties litigation remains active.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing can turn ordinary screening, facility, schooling, or care disputes into enforcement or investigation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minors are barred from congruent facilities and sports; care denial can implicate parents and providers; school or medical encounters may trigger state inquiry or separation of care.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented family-facing protection in the division; local ordinances are uncertain.
minors_guardians.interaction: Enrollment, sports, prescriptions, emergency treatment, or ID checks can out the child and expose the guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific attack rate or incident in the division; an undercount figure is not evidence. Police may treat ID mismatch as fraud or mishandle complaints.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute offers theoretical recourse; local bias statutes are absent.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Lack of state recourse may deter reporting, while hostile climate can raise risk without proving frequency.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and facility orders are contested; enforcement varies; no documented effective visitor remedy for division bans or immigration custody abuse.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal aid, civil-liberties suits, court injunctions, and some local ordinances may help after harm.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown current rules and slow remedies mean travellers cannot safely predict exposure; absence of evidence is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar birth-sex document and facility enforcement, but worse: visa fraud lifetime findings, immigration-custody abuse, care criminalization for minors, and no statewide recourse; slightly below.
Border refusal and humiliation are present, but this combined regime adds criminal facility exposure, custody placement, abuse, and family care denial; clearly below.
Far below an entry regime with trained respectful screening and remedies; here border and visa screening is hostile, ID mismatch can escalate, and facilities and care are restrictive.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime compounds at every journey stage: home documents meet birth-sex visa screening, airport security can force disclosure, then state/province facilities and binary-identity laws turn everyday movement into an outing risk. If the traveller is detained or arrested, custody placement and documented sexual abuse or forced labour create severe consequences; for minors, provider felony and school investigations make family travel especially dangerous. National hate-crime law and litigation give some recourse, but they do not change border, facility, care, or custody practice here. Violence frequency remains uncertain and the trans-women killing-rate figure is an unusable undercount floor, so no campaign is proven; however absence of evidence is not safety. Combined, this is a high-risk jurisdiction with severe universal exposures and weak remedies, not execution-level.
